source.version: abstract only (Crossref record for DOI 10.2139/ssrn.4751779, SSRN working paper, 2024); no full text on file, SSRN page returned HTTP 403; OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar records carry no abstract
source.title_on_document: How AI Outperforms Humans at Creative Idea Generation

paper_design_summary: The abstract compares the rated creativity of GPT-4-generated new product ideas with ideas from laypeople and creative professionals working under strong financial incentives and describes text-analysis measures of creative form (unusual language) and creative substance (novelty of the idea). It also compares GPT-4 rewrites of human-written ideas with the originals. These are provisionally AI-versus-human output comparisons; human access to AI and assignment to assistance are not stated, and the full paper's study structure is unverified.

studies.label: GPT-4 product ideas vs ideas from laypeople and creative professionals

participants.who: Human idea generators: laypeople and creative professionals working under strong financial incentives. The abstract gives no counts and does not say who rated the ideas.
participants.quote: GPT4 can generate ideas that are rated as more creative than those generated by laypeople and creative professionals working under strong financial incentives

ai_tool.how_used: The abstract describes GPT-4-generated new product ideas compared with human-generated ideas; who operated GPT-4, human access to AI, and assignment to assistance are not stated.

outcomes.name: Rated creativity of ideas
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: The abstract says the ideas were 'rated as more creative'; it does not say who rated them (people or a model) or on what scale.

contrasts.control_arm: Ideas from laypeople and from creative professionals working under strong financial incentives
contrasts.reported: No numbers in the abstract. Text: 'GPT4 can generate ideas that are rated as more creative than those generated by laypeople and creative professionals working under strong financial incentives.'

outcomes.name: Creative form (unusual or unique language describing the idea)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Measure from the authors' 'novel text analysis methodology'; the abstract defines creative form as 'the language used to describe an idea being more unusual or unique'. Method details not in the abstract.

contrasts.reported: No numbers in the abstract. Text: 'We find that GPT4 outperforms humans in both types of creativity.'

outcomes.name: Creative substance (novelty of the idea itself)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Measure from the authors' text analysis; the abstract defines creative substance as 'the idea itself is more novel'. Method details not in the abstract.

contrasts.reported: No numbers in the abstract. Text: 'We find that GPT4 outperforms humans in both types of creativity.'

studies.label: GPT-4 rewrites of human-written ideas vs the human originals

participants.who: Ideas 'originally written by humans' (abstract does not say which humans or how many), rewritten by GPT-4. Raters not described.
participants.quote: using GPT4 to simply re-write ideas originally written by humans results in those ideas being rated as significantly more creative

ai_tool.how_used: The abstract describes GPT-4 rewrites of human-written ideas; who operated GPT-4, whether the human authors used it, and assignment to assistance are not stated.

task.description: Re-writing of human-written new product ideas.

outcomes.name: Rated creativity of GPT-4-rewritten ideas vs original human versions
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: The abstract says the rewrites were 'rated as significantly more creative' and that 'the improvement is explained by creativity in form'; it does not say who rated them.

contrasts.treatment_arm: GPT-4 rewrite of a human-written idea
contrasts.reported: No numbers in the abstract. Text: 'rated as significantly more creative and that the improvement is explained by creativity in form.'

eligibility.reason: The Crossref abstract for DOI 10.2139/ssrn.4751779 (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.2139/ssrn.4751779, sentences beginning We first demonstrate and Finally) describes GPT-4 ideas and rewrites compared with human-written ideas, supporting provisional ai_vs_human context classification and confirming creativity scored on output. It gives no assignment procedures or people counts, and human access to AI is unspecified; criteria 1 and 2 and paper-wide core eligibility remain unclear. No randomized people study is identified in the abstract, but its absence from the complete paper is not established. No full text is on file, and the SSRN page returned HTTP 403. The search notes mention a related Marketing Science paper; whether it reports the same studies is unconfirmed.

one_line_finding: GPT-4 product ideas were rated more creative than ideas from laypeople and incentivized creative professionals, outperformed humans on both text-based creative form and creative substance, and GPT-4 rewrites of human ideas were rated significantly more creative (abstract, Crossref; no numbers in the abstract).
